title: Vegan Coconut Cloud Cupcakes
shortDescription: These vegan coconut cupcakes need 25 minutes of prep and bake in 18 minutes, topped with a fluffy coconut whip frosting.
description: I wanted a coconut cupcake that actually tastes like coconut, not just a hint of it. This batter uses full fat coconut milk in place of dairy milk, so every bite is soft and moist. The frosting is whipped coconut cream with a touch of vanilla, light as a cloud. I tested this recipe three times in my home kitchen to get the crumb right. The trick is chilling the coconut milk can overnight so the cream separates and whips up thick. No coconut oil needed for the frosting, just cold cream and patience. These are great for spring parties or anyone avoiding dairy and eggs. The toasted coconut on top adds crunch against the soft frosting. Kids and adults both ask for seconds. If you like tropical flavors, this recipe pairs well with my mango coconut cupcakes too. Swap the vanilla for almond extract if you want a slightly different finish.
ingredients: 1 cup full fat coconut milk, well shaken
1/2 cup unsweetened shredded coconut, plus 1/4 cup for topping
2 cans (13.5 oz each) full fat coconut milk, chilled overnight
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix coconut milk, oil, vanilla, and apple cider vinegar.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir until just combined, no lumps.
Fold in 1/2 cup shredded coconut. Do not overmix the batter.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Open chilled coconut milk cans and scoop out only the thick cream on top.
Whip the coconut cream with powdered sugar and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Pipe or spread frosting onto fully cooled cupcakes.
Sprinkle toasted shredded coconut on top before serving.
tips: Chill your coconut milk cans for at least 12 hours so the cream separates properly.
Toast the shredded coconut in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes for extra flavor.
Do not shake the chilled cans before opening, or the cream will mix back into the liquid.
Store leftover cupcakes in the fridge since the frosting is cream based.

faq.question: Why is my coconut whip frosting runny?
faq.answer: Your coconut milk was probably not chilled long enough. Chill the cans for a full 12 hours and only scoop the solid cream layer, not the liquid underneath.

faq.question: Can I use light coconut milk instead of full fat?
faq.answer: No, light coconut milk does not have enough cream to whip into frosting. Use full fat coconut milk for both the batter and the frosting.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted at room temperature. Whip the frosting fresh and pipe it the day you plan to serve them.

faq.question: Do these cupcakes need to stay refrigerated?
faq.answer: Yes, once frosted with coconut whip they should go in the fridge. Bring them to room temperature for about 20 minutes before serving for the best texture.

conclusion: These coconut cupcakes prove vegan baking can still feel rich and soft. Keep the coconut milk cold, do not overmix, and you get a light crumb every time.
